newsitem.title: USA: Wall St stocks seen rising at open.
newsitem.headline: Wall St stocks seen rising at open.

text.p: U.S. stocks are expected to push higher at Wednesday's open, a day after the Dow industrials finally managed to close over the 5900 level.
Blue chips had met with stubborn resistance in several previous runs at the marker and their success yesterday seemed to spark renewed interest in U.S. stocks.

"Yesterday's rally carried over into London," said Larry Wachtel, market analyst at Prudential Securities. "It looks like we'll have a fairly good open and now it's a matter of internal dynamics and whether we can carry it forward."
The session will see a light load of economic input, with only August construction spending data due at 1000 EDT/1400 GMT. Economists forecase a 0.8 percent rise versus July's 1.4 percent decline.
With key employment figures not due until Friday and a firm bond market pushing interest rates lower, analysts said stocks might quickly take a run at the 6000 mark.

"It looks as though rates may trade down to the 6.75 percent level before the unemployment number Friday," said Peter Cardillo, director of research at Westfalia Investments. "If that's the case we may be headed for 6000 in the Dow."

The Dow could get a boost from recent laggard AT&T Corp, which early this morning announced its much-awaited personal communications services (PCS) offering, which combines voice, messaging and paging services.
AT&T shares traded slightly higher in London ahead of the announcement.
In Tokyo, stocks edged higher after wandering in a narrow range for most of the session. The Nikkei-225 index rose about 36 points to 21,499.
U.S. stocks were firmer across the board in London and the FTSE-100 gained 20 points to 4012, piercing the 4000 mark.

The dollar gained ground in Tokyo, hitting a 33-month high against the Japanese yen but holding just short of the 112 yen level. Caution ahead of Friday's unemployment and payrolls figures held the dollar in check in Europe.
U.S. Treasuries were slightly higher. The benchmark 30-year bond gained 2/32 to yield 6.87 percent.
The December S&P 500 index future rose 1.25 to 696.35.
The New York Times Marketplace Column focuses on the sharp sell-off in HCIA Inc that followed the company's earnings warning.

The Wall Street Journal's Heard on the Street column notes that Planet Hollywood International Inc shares are sporting an extremely high price to earnings ratio and reports several mutual funds have sold their shares in the company.
